belief.answer:
Put N=binom(n,2), H=(n^(n−2))!, B=2^(N+n), and δ(x)=floor(1/(|x|+1)). For 0≤b<2^N, let A_b be the symmetric zero-diagonal n×n matrix whose upper-triangular entries, in lexicographic order, are the binary digits of b starting with the least significant digit. Define d_{b,i}=∑_j(A_b)_{ij} and L_b=diag(d_{b,1},…,d_{b,n})−A_b. Write L_b^[S] for the matrix obtained by deleting rows and columns in S, and set a_b=det L_b^[{n}], f_{b,uv}=det L_b^[{u,v}], q_b=a_b+δ(a_b), and w_b=(1−δ(a_b))∏_{i=2}^n δ(d_{b,i}−d_{b,1}). An explicit exact formula, valid throughout the requested domain, is
\[\boxed{\displaystyle t_n=\frac1H\left\lfloor\log_B\!\left(1+\sum_{b=0}^{2^N-1}w_b\sum_{1\le u<v\le n}B^{\,Hn d_{b,1}f_{b,uv}/q_b}\right)\right\rfloor.}\]

options.approach: Search specifically among graphs with no bridges or articulation vertices, then compare their exact commute times with the block-chain constructions. This would test whether small edge cuts, rather than single-vertex or single-edge bottlenecks, provide better extremizers.
